investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Gateway 502 on POST /api/agents (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-01T15:04–15:05Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was unreachable during agent provisioning. The eval runner's POST /api/agents call never received a successful response, so zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and every contract assertion was unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every attempt. Because the failure occurs before the agent is created, no evidence can be written and all downstream contract assertions fail as a consequence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency of POST /api/agents; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

[Possible] The swarm service behind the ELB was restarting or had crashed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy instances and returning 502 to all upstream callers.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a hard error (code: credit_balance_exhausted). The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions failed: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false. This is an eval infrastructure / API credential failure, not a confirmed user-facing product outage.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI API key configured for the eval environment has exhausted its credit balance. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1984), the upstream OpenAI request was rejected with type=insufficient_quota and code=credit_balance_exhausted. The stream emitted generation_error instead of generation_completed, causing both required contract assertions to fail (failed-check.message, failed-check.evidence).
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error type=insufficient_quota, code=credit_balance_exhausted — the upstream API explicitly rejected the request due to zero remaining credits.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent=false — both contract assertions violated.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1644 — the stream failed in under 2 seconds, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation failure.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985 (line 1984): runner calls apiSse to /api/generate/image/stream; the error propagated from that call.

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent equals true — neither was satisfied.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:335-343 (lines 341-343): contract definition confirms the two required assertions that failed.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — The OpenAI API key used by the eval runner environment has a zero or negative credit balance, causing all image generation requests to be rejected immediately with credit_balance_exhausted.
SECONDARY — The eval runner is using a separate, lower-quota API key (e.g. a test/CI key distinct from the production key) that has run out of credits while the production key may still have balance.
TERTIARY — A billing threshold or spending cap was hit on the OpenAI organization account referenced by the eval key, blocking new requests even if the account has a positive nominal balance.

UNLIKELY — A misconfigured or rotated API key is being used that belongs to an organization with no credits; the error message is explicit about credit exhaustion rather than authentication failure, making a key misconfiguration less likely but not impossible.
